questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “You must follow these rules.”
questions.why: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

opts: She is more intelligent of the two sisters.
She is the more intelligent of the two sisters.
She is the most intelligenter of the two sisters.
She is the most intelligent of the two sisters.
questions.why: With two, use the comparative with 'the': 'the more … of the two'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “He prevented me ______ going out.”
Choose the correct article: “She is working as ____ university lecturer.”
questions.why: 'University' begins with the consonant sound /j/. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “This is the third time he ______ late this week.”
questions.why: 'This is the first/second/third time' takes the present perfect. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct conjunction: “Not only did he fail the test, ____ he also lost the scholarship.”
questions.why: Correlative pair: not only ... but also. GPSC-style practice item.

opts: If he left earlier, he would have caught the train.
If he would have left earlier, he would have caught the train.
If he had left earlier, he would have caught the train.
If he had left earlier, he would catch the train yesterday.
questions.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Never 'would have' in the if-clause. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. It spreads through contaminated water.
Q. Cholera is a serious bacterial disease.
R. Therefore, safe drinking water is essential for prevention.
S. Untreated, it can cause severe dehydration and even death.
questions.why: Introduce the disease, its spread and effect, then the conclusion with 'Therefore'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the clause type: “What the doctor said surprised everyone.”
questions.why: The clause is the subject of 'surprised', so it is a noun clause. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.
